study type: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
cohort: The study included 2035 women with a prepregnancy body mass index >=30 kg/m2 undergoing cesarean delivery.
finding: Wound complications and surgical wound dehiscence were high in this population, with predictors including 1 previous cesarean delivery and ruptured membranes >12 hours, while vaginal cleansing, low transverse incision, and double-layer uterine closure were associated with decreased odds of complications.
